issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency: In the solution implementation of class Lecture the field declarations use snake_case identifiers (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while the constructor, getters/setters, toString, and other methods in the same solution file reference camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The problem statement UML also specifies camelCase field names. This mismatch between declared field names and referenced names will cause compilation errors and prevents students from using the solution as a correct reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make identifier names consistent. Prefer matching the UML/problem statement: rename the solution's snake_case fields to camelCase (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) so they match the constructor, getters, setters and toString. Alternatively (less preferred), update all uses in the solution to the snake_case names. Ensure the final names match the UML and compile without errors.

issues.description: The exercise UML and problem text define five lecture attributes using camelCase identifiers: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. In the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) the fields are declared using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) but the constructor and methods reference camelCase names (e.g., this.lectureName, getNumberOfTutors()). This mismatch means the declared field identifiers do not match the identifiers used elsewhere in the class, will cause compilation errors, and breaks the direct mapping from the UML/problem to the implementation — creating confusion for students and preventing the solution from compiling as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifiers consistent. Rename the solution's snake_case fields to the camelCase names used in the UML/problem (e.g., change 'private String lecture_name;' to 'private String lectureName;' and similarly for numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), and ensure the constructor, getters, setters and methods reference those same camelCase fields. Alternatively, consistently replace all usages with the snake_case names, but prefer aligning the solution to the UML's camelCase to match the exercise and the template.
